whyThisMatters: These aren't just buzzwords — knowing what phishing, MFA, or ransomware actually mean is what lets you recognize the real thing the moment it shows up in your inbox or on your screen.
rememberThis: You don't need to memorize a glossary — just enough of these words to recognize the real thing when it shows up.

wordlist.clue: A fake message designed to trick you into clicking or sharing information
General term for any software built to damage, spy on, or take over a device
Malware that locks your files and demands payment before you can get them back
You enter your password, then approve a prompt on your phone — that second step is called this
The secret combination of characters that proves it's really you logging in
The security layer that filters traffic in and out of a network, blocking what looks dangerous
You connect to airport WiFi and switch this on first to encrypt your traffic
Scrambling data so that only someone with the right key can read it
A social engineering trick where the attacker invents a false scenario, like posing as IT support
What happens when sensitive data is exposed or stolen from a system — a data ___
Software that scans your device and removes known malicious programs
A saved copy of your files that lets you recover after ransomware or a crash
Your control over who can see or use your personal information
Malware that disguises itself as a legitimate program to get you to install it
Faking a sender address or caller ID so a message looks like it's from someone you trust
The update you keep postponing that actually fixes a known security hole
A network of hijacked devices controlled remotely to launch attacks together
Unwanted bulk email or messages, sometimes just annoying, sometimes carrying malware
